newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed on select blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed on select blue-chip buying.

text.p: Select blue-chip buying by funds pushed up the key Composite Index, but small cap shares retreated on profit-taking, brokers and analysts said.
They said the market was worried that the stock exchange may query some sharp rises in small cap shares on Wednesday after it imposed trading restrictions on Zaitun.
The Composite Index ended up 9.36 points at 1,097.48, while the second board was down 3.07 at 578.16.
"Much of the activity was speculative, though some funds were nibbling on the blue-chips," said a dealer with a bank-backed brokerage in Kuala Lumpur.
He said the volume was pretty thin, but the fact that the Composite Index ended up gave hope that it could go past 1,100 before the week was out.
Dealers said small-cap shares were mainly being sold by syndicates, who were scared that some of the shares pushed up on Wednesday may attract the stock exchange's attention.
Zaitun shares, which gained five ringgit on Wednesday, fell 3.45 ringgit to 9.05. The shares were listed last week at 6.55 ringgit against an offer price of 2.10.
LKT Industrial on the second board bucked the trend to continue rising. It ended up 1.80 ringgit at 20.30.
"There is a rumour about a reverse takeover at LKT, which why it is in play," said a dealer with a retail-based brokerage.
Eden Enterprises led the list of actives after being requoted on Thursday. It was suspended on Wednesday by the stock exchange due to the heavy volume in its shares.
Eden ended down 40 cents at 7.95 ringgit.
Maybank continued gaining on accumulation of the stock ahead of the results. It is widely rumoured to be heading for better-than-expected profit in the year to June 30, 1997.
Index heavyweights, Telekom rose 30 cents to 12.10 ringgit and Tenaga was up 10 cents at 12 ringgit.
